beats.title: Edwin Smith Papyrus Maps the Brain
beats.description: An Egyptian surgical text gives the first known written description of the brain, its membranes and the effects of head wounds.
beats.note: Copied c. 1600 BCE from older text; year approximate

beats.title: Hippocratics Put Mind in the Brain
beats.description: Greek physicians of the Hippocratic school declare that the brain, not the heart, is the seat of thought, joy and madness.
beats.note: c. 400 BCE, approximate (On the Sacred Disease)

beats.title: Bethlem Takes Its First Patients
beats.description: A London priory begins to house the mentally ill and becomes the infamous asylum that gave the language the word bedlam.
beats.note: Became a hospital for the mentally ill later; 1247 is the standard founding year

beats.title: Valencia Opens an Asylum
beats.description: A Spanish priest founds an institution devoted to caring for the insane, often named as Europe's first psychiatric hospital.

beats.title: Weyer Says Witches Are Ill
beats.description: A Dutch physician publishes a book arguing that many accused witches suffer from mental illness and need medicine, not punishment.

beats.title: The Anatomy of Melancholy Appears
beats.description: An Oxford scholar publishes an enormous, learned study of depression, its causes and cures, which stays in print for centuries.

beats.title: Willis Publishes Brain Anatomy
beats.description: An English physician publishes the most detailed map of the brain and nerves yet seen and helps found the science of neurology.

beats.title: Mesmer Begins Magnetic Cures
beats.description: A Viennese doctor starts treating patients with supposed magnetic fluids, launching the craze that later led to hypnosis.

beats.title: Pinel Unchains the Insane
beats.description: A French physician orders the chains removed from patients at a Paris asylum, treating them as sick people rather than beasts.

beats.title: The York Retreat Opens
beats.description: English Quakers open a gentle country retreat for the mentally ill, pioneering kindness and routine instead of restraint.

beats.title: Gall Launches Phrenology
beats.description: A German physician argues that mental faculties live in distinct parts of the brain and can be read from the skull's bumps.
beats.note: Gall's major work with Spurzheim began 1810

beats.title: Dix Petitions for the Insane
beats.description: An American reformer presents a stark report on the neglect of mentally ill people, sparking a wave of new state hospitals.
beats.note: Memorial to the Massachusetts legislature, January

beats.title: Phineas Gage's Accident
beats.description: An iron rod blasts through a railway foreman's skull and he survives, but his personality is said to change dramatically.

beats.title: Broca Finds the Speech Area
beats.description: A French surgeon links damage in one region of a patient's left frontal brain to the loss of speech.

beats.title: Golgi Stains the Nerve Cell
beats.description: An Italian scientist invents a silver stain that reveals whole neurons under the microscope for the first time.

beats.title: Wernicke Finds the Language Area
beats.description: A German neurologist describes a brain region whose damage leaves patients speaking fluently but without meaning.

beats.title: Wundt Opens First Psychology Lab
beats.description: A German professor founds a laboratory in Leipzig devoted to measuring the mind, marking psychology as an experimental science.

beats.title: Kraepelin Classifies Mental Illness
beats.description: A German psychiatrist publishes a textbook sorting mental disorders into types, the root of modern psychiatric diagnosis.

beats.title: Cajal Shows the Neuron Is Separate
beats.description: A Spanish anatomist draws nerve cells as individual units rather than a continuous web, founding the neuron doctrine.
beats.note: Key 1888 Golgi-stain studies of the cerebellum; not re-searched

beats.title: James's Principles of Psychology
beats.description: A Harvard thinker's two-volume work introduces the stream of consciousness and shapes the new science of mind.

beats.title: Freud's Interpretation of Dreams
beats.description: A Viennese doctor argues that dreams are disguised wishes, launching the theory of the unconscious that became psychoanalysis.
beats.note: Published November 1899, dated 1900 on title page

beats.title: Binet's Intelligence Test
beats.description: A French psychologist and his colleague create the first practical test to identify children needing extra help in school.

beats.title: Alzheimer Presents His First Case
beats.description: A German psychiatrist describes a woman with memory loss whose brain shows strange plaques and tangles after death.

beats.title: Watson's Behaviorist Manifesto
beats.description: An American psychologist declares that psychology should study only observable behaviour, not introspection.
beats.note: Psychology as the Behaviorist Views It; not re-searched

beats.title: Little Albert Learns to Fear
beats.description: Researchers teach a baby to fear a white rat by pairing it with a loud noise, a notorious demonstration of learned emotion.

beats.title: Rorschach's Inkblot Test
beats.description: A Swiss psychiatrist publishes ten symmetrical inkblots that people interpret, meant to reveal hidden personality traits.

beats.title: Moniz Performs the First Lobotomy
beats.description: A Portuguese neurologist has surgeons cut into the frontal lobes of a patient to treat mental illness, a method later much condemned.

beats.title: First Electroconvulsive Therapy
beats.description: Italian doctors give a patient with schizophrenia a brief electric shock to the head to induce a therapeutic seizure.

beats.title: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
beats.description: An American psychologist arranges human motivations in a pyramid from food and safety up to self-fulfilment.

beats.title: Cade Treats Mania with Lithium
beats.description: An Australian psychiatrist discovers that a simple salt calms patients with manic episodes, beginning modern mood-stabiliser therapy.
beats.note: Published 1949; some sources give 1948 for the discovery

beats.title: Chlorpromazine Calms Psychosis
beats.description: French doctors find a drug that calms psychosis, emptying the wards of straitjackets and starting the age of psychiatric medicine.

beats.title: Patient H.M. Loses His Memory
beats.description: Surgery to cure a man's epilepsy removes parts of both temporal lobes and leaves him unable to form new memories.

beats.title: Milgram's Obedience Experiment
beats.description: Volunteers are told to give what they think are painful shocks to a stranger, and most keep obeying the experimenter.

beats.title: Kubler-Ross Describes Grief Stages
beats.description: A Swiss-American psychiatrist publishes a bestseller describing five stages people pass through when facing death.

beats.title: The Stanford Prison Experiment
beats.description: Students playing guards and prisoners in a basement mock jail turn cruel so quickly that the study is stopped early.

beats.title: Rosenhan's Pseudopatients
beats.description: Healthy volunteers feign hearing voices to enter psychiatric hospitals, then act normally but stay for weeks.

beats.title: DSM-III Remakes Diagnosis
beats.description: The American psychiatric manual adopts precise symptom checklists for each disorder and sets the model for diagnosis worldwide.

beats.title: Gardner's Multiple Intelligences
beats.description: A Harvard psychologist argues that intelligence has several independent forms, such as musical, spatial and interpersonal.

beats.title: Prozac Reaches the Market
beats.description: An American drug company launches a new antidepressant that becomes one of the most prescribed and talked-about medicines ever.

beats.title: Mirror Neurons Are Reported
beats.description: Italian researchers find brain cells in monkeys that fire both when the animal acts and when it watches another act.
beats.note: First described 1992; named in 1996 paper, which is the year used

beats.title: Optogenetics Switches Neurons
beats.description: Researchers show that light-sensitive proteins let them turn chosen brain cells on and off with flashes of light.
beats.note: First experiment 2004; published 2005, which is the year used

beats.title: The BRAIN Initiative Is Announced
beats.description: The United States launches a large public research programme to map brain activity and understand how circuits produce thought.
